title: Characterization of a damping channel as a mixture of amplitude damping and anti-damping channels of different parameters
abstract: Non-unital noise is a fundamental feature of open quantum systems, governing energy exchange and inducing state translations on the Bloch sphere. While such translations can be useful for tasks such as state preparation and channel capacity, unital dynamics where no translation occurs are often preferred in quantum information processing, particularly for error correction. Phase-covariant dynamics provide a general framework encompassing dissipation, excitation, and dephasing processes in qubit systems; however, commonly used models such as the generalized amplitude damping (GAD) channel offer only limited control over these features. In this work, we present a constructive framework for generating a broader class of phase-covariant dynamics by mixing amplitude-damping and anti-damping channels with unequal decay parameters and time-dependent mixing probabilities. This approach enables independent control over contraction and translation, allows continuous tuning between non-unital and unital regimes, and yields an effective dephasing contribution absent in GAD. To characterize these dynamics, we employ the general theorem for P-divisibility and show that it can be used constructively by evaluating it in suitably chosen Hilbert space bases, leading to simplified conditions for both unital and non-unital cases. The framework captures a wide range of behaviors, including CP-divisible, P-divisible but not CP-divisible, and non-P-divisible dynamics. We further show that appropriate mixing can reduce the deviation from the ideal noiseless evolution and that such improvement persists even after tuning the dynamics to the unital regime. Our results provide a flexible approach to engineering open system dynamics beyond standard thermal models, with potential applications in noise control and quantum information processing.
summary: This paper presents a novel method to engineer open quantum system dynamics by mixing amplitude-damping and anti-damping channels. This framework grants independent control over different aspects of decoherence, allowing researchers to tune dynamics between unital and non-unital regimes. The results offer a flexible tool for quantum information processing, enabling precise control over noise mitigation and channel characterization.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a constructive framework to generate a broad class of phase-covariant quantum dynamics that goes beyond standard models like Generalized Amplitude Damping (GAD). This allows for independent control over different aspects of open system evolution.
main_result: The proposed mixing of amplitude-damping and anti-damping channels allows for independent control over contraction and translation of the Bloch sphere, enabling the engineering of dynamics with specific divisibility properties (P-divisible, CP-divisible).
method: The authors employ the general theorem for P-divisibility and CP-divisibility, applying it constructively by mixing two known channels (AD and anti-AD) with time-dependent probabilities and parameters.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a qubit undergoing open evolution, governed by a general master equation in the phase-covariant class. The dynamics are characterized by time-dependent rates ($\gamma_{\pm}(t), \gamma_z(t)$).
key_observables: P-divisibility, CP-divisibility, the trace norm distance $D(t)$ from the identity channel, and the evolution of Bloch sphere coordinates.
important_parameters: Unequal decay parameters ($\eta_1(t), \eta_2(t)$) for the two channels, and the time-dependent mixing probability $p(t)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the dynamics are completely positive (CP) from $t=0$, and the primary utility relies on the controllable anti-AD channel exhibiting complete recurrence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of the error metric $D(t)$ and the translation term, comparing results for various combinations of AD/anti-AD parameters and mixing probabilities.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem, introduces the mixing framework, derives necessary and sufficient conditions for P-divisibility using specialized bases, and finally demonstrates the control over error mitigation and dynamical regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, flexible tool for quantum information scientists to engineer noise channels, moving beyond simple thermal models to precisely control decoherence effects for error correction or state preparation.

FIG. 4: The P-divisibility condition is plotted as a function of time for η1(t) = exp[−χ1t] and η2(t) = exp[−χ2ti] with constant mixing probability p. The different curves correspond to different values of the exponent i. The condition remains positive throughout the evolution for i ≤3, indicating P-divisible dynamics, whereas for i > 3 it becomes negative over part of the evolution, indicating non-P-divisible dynamics.

Top left: all three canonical rates remain positive, corresponding to CP-divisible dynamics.
